title: The Tenth Wedding
logline: Kiran shows the room two unopened folds and the real numbers, and the gang stops obeying Mausi; Mausi bares the scar to Aditya to turn him on her, and Kiran takes the keys, sends him home alive with nothing, and by evening is teaching the next bride to pour.
language_note: en-IN: Indian English, same cast as the Hinglish cut. Kept as spoken in India: Mausi, beta, Damaad ji, meri bachchi, Didi, tola, tawa.

characters.name: Kiran
characters.role: LEAD. The bureau's vanishing bride. Tonight she faked the fatal dose; by evening she runs the bureau.
characters.look: Indian woman, 27, about 5 ft 3, slight and wiry. Wheat-brown skin, oval face, straight dark brows, large kajal-lined eyes, a closed, watchful mouth. Low bun, sindoor, small red bindi, thin gold ring in the left nostril, block henna on both hands. b1 to b7: plain sindoor-red saree with a thin gold border, barefoot, red-and-ivory chooda on both forearms; from b4 the LEFT stack is pushed up toward the elbow and the crescent scar stays bare (story_locks.scar), she never pulls it down; from b6 Mausi's steel key ring is knotted at her left hip. b9 to b10 (period 3): plain ash-grey salwar-kurta and grey dupatta, both forearms bare with faint pressure lines where the bangles sat, the crescent on the outer LEFT forearm, the key ring at her left hip.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Female, late 20s, alto with a dry edge. Indian English of a small-city Madhya Pradesh woman who learnt it at school and from a phone: simple, quick, contractions, a light Hindi accent, no British or American colour. Keeps Mausi, Didi. Low, flat, quick, short sentences. Under pressure she gets quieter and more exact, never shrill. By the bureau scene her pace has slowed into Mausi's unhurried warmth.

characters.name: Aditya Verma
characters.role: The groom. Mohit's brother. Pretended to drink the dose; tonight he sees the hand and can do nothing with it.
characters.look: Indian man, 33, about 6 ft, tall and narrow, slight stoop. Light-brown skin, long clean-shaven face, neat left-parted black hair, rimless rectangular glasses on in every shot. Plain cream cotton-silk wedding kurta and churidar, creased; barefoot in the bedroom, tan leather sandals on the stairs and in the lane. Brass key about 5 cm long on a doubled red thread outside the kurta at mid-chest, in every shot. Plain steel watch, brown strap, left wrist, never readable.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Male, early 30s, light baritone, soft-spoken. Careful Indian English of a small-city science graduate: complete sentences, precise nouns, no slang, a light Hindi accent, no British or American colour. Under pressure he slows down and drops in volume; never shouts. The one place the voice may catch is the single word in b5.

characters.name: Shakun Mausi
characters.role: Owner of the bureau. Ordered Aditya's death tonight. Loses the keys and is set to writing the accounts.
characters.look: Indian woman, 56, about 5 ft 2, broad and heavy-shouldered. Brown skin, round face, heavy-lidded shrewd eyes, paan-reddened smile, large round maroon bindi, small gold nose stud, grey-streaked hair in a tight oiled bun. Starched bottle-green cotton saree with a narrow mustard border, mustard blouse, thin gold chain, rubber slippers, a dozen green glass bangles on each wrist. Steel ring of about eight keys at her LEFT hip in b1 to b5; none from b6 on.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Female, mid 50s, low, warm and grainy, a paan-chewer's unhurried mouth. Warm, motherly Indian English with a strong Hindi accent, short plain sentences, Hindi endearments kept (beta, Damaad ji, meri bachchi); she sounds like someone's aunt at a wedding. No British or American colour. Never raises her voice: the colder the move, the softer and slower she gets. Fully voiced, never a whisper.

characters.name: Billu
characters.role: Mausi's driver and the bride's 'brother'. Learns in numbers how long he has been short-changed and stops obeying her.
characters.look: Indian man, 30, about 5 ft 7, wiry, brown skin, sharp jaw, patchy stubble, hair gelled straight back. Faded blue denim jacket, sleeves pushed up, over a black T-shirt; dark jeans; grey-white sneakers. Wooden toothpick in the right corner of his mouth until b3, when he takes it out; out for the rest of the episode. Car key on a plain steel ring hooked on his right index finger. No weapon.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Male, about 30, light tenor, fast, a little nasal. Quick, slangy Indian English of a small-town Bundelkhand driver with a strong Hindi accent, an article dropped now and then; keeps Mausi. Never American street slang, never British. When surprised he goes loud for one line, then looks to Mausi. Once the numbers land, his pace drops and the jokes stop.

characters.name: The boys
characters.look: Never a face. Two fixed shapes: heavy-set, shaved head, maroon track jacket; thin, checked shirt, cloth cap. Backs, hands, boots and backlit silhouettes only, heads cropped, turned away or in full shadow.
characters.voice_note: No lines. Any breath or shuffle is a sound effect.

characters.name: Chhoti
characters.role: The next bride. Her first wedding is tomorrow.
characters.look: Adult woman, 19, about 5 ft 1, slight, wide curious eyes, light-brown skin. One long black braid pulled forward over her right shoulder. Plain mustard-yellow cotton kurta, white salwar, a plain dupatta (D-007 direction 14). Henna finished on both palms. Kiran's red-and-ivory chooda on both forearms. Phone in a plain pink cover in her right hand.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Female, 19, a young woman's voice, not a child's: bright, quick, sing-song, a giggle in the breath. Light, eager small-town Indian English in short sentences, keeps Didi; no British or American colour. Here the giggle is put on over fear.

location: Four places: the rented house's bedroom (b1 to b6), its stairwell (b7) and the lane outside (b8) at dawn, then Shubh Lagan Marriage Bureau's front room the same evening (b9 to b10).
time_of_day: Night 1, about 5:05 am to first light (b1 to b8). Bedroom light state 3 for b1 to b6 (amber lamp, the landing bulb through the open door, pre-dawn blue at the window grille, greying toward dawn by b6); first grey light in the stairwell (b7) and the lane (b8). Day 2, evening (b9 to b10).

beats.action: Opens inside s1b02's last image. Light: state 3, as at the end of s1b02: amber lamp, the landing bulb through the open door, pre-dawn blue at the window grille, greying toward dawn by b6. On the sheet by Aditya's hip, the small black notebook, closed on the creased photograph, where Mausi left it (s1b01 b11). Set-up 1 (the 1.2 s silence): insert, close behind Kiran's back, red saree: her LEFT hand palm up on the henna disc, two paper folds still folded shut on it, the chooda at rest over the wrist. Set-up 2 (l01 only): Mausi turned away from the bed toward the door, keys at her left hip, talking over her shoulder to Billu. Set-up 3 (from the start of l02): Billu, toothpick in, steps toward the bed where Aditya lies among the marigolds, eyes shut, glasses on, brass key on its red thread, the closed notebook by his hip. Mausi's half-turn toward Kiran on 'Come, beta' is not shown; the key chink carries it (sfx_notes). The boys are two backlit shapes by the door, heads out of frame.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] Shut the door, Billu. Let the landlord find him in the morning.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] Come, beta. Home.

beats.action: Set-up 1 (the 0.5 s silence, l03): Kiran steps into Billu's path between him and the bed; two-shot Kiran and Billu, her left fist now closed at her side. Set-up 2 (l04): single on Kiran, low and exact. Set-up 3 (l31): single on Billu, toothpick still in, eyes sliding to Mausi. Set-up 4 (l05): Kiran single, REUSE of the set-up 2 frame; on 'Mohit's', insert: Aditya's face on the pillow, eyes shut behind the glasses; the one change is his jaw tightening. Set-up 5 (l06): Billu single, REUSE of the set-up 3 frame (or a 1.3x punch-in on it). Set-up 6 (l07 up to 'car'): Kiran, closer, a 1.3x PUNCH-IN on the set-up 2 frame. Set-up 7 (from 'car' through l08): new insert, Billu's car key on its plain steel ring hooked on his right index finger. Set-up 8 (l09): Billu, loud for one line, turning to Mausi. Set-up 9 (l10): Mausi single, smiling, softer than ever. The boys stay backs and silhouettes at frame edge. No frame holds more than two sheet faces.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [quietly] Wait, Billu. Check the accounts first.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] Last party, twenty-two tola. Say it in front of Mausi. How much did she tell you?

lines.speaker: billu
lines.text: [nervous] Twelve.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [quietly] And at Mohit's wedding, his mother's gold bangles. Nine tola.

lines.speaker: billu
lines.text: [nervous] Mausi told me it was four.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] Every time, she told you half. And the car's in your name.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [sharply] Tonight's body was going on your head too.

lines.speaker: billu
lines.text: [angry] Mausi, is she telling the truth?

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [quietly] The poor child is tired, Billu.

beats.action: Set-up 1 (first sentence of l11): insert, Kiran holds her LEFT hand out palm up: two folds, unopened. Set-up 2 (from 'The fresh milk Billu brought' through l33): Aditya opens his eyes and sits up among the marigolds, glasses and key on; Kiran, if in frame, is a back only. Set-up 3 (l12): two-shot Kiran and Billu; Kiran's fist closes on the folds again. The 2.0 s silence after l12 is two set-ups of 1 s: the boys' boots stepping back toward the door (feet and calves only); Billu single, taking the toothpick out of his mouth.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] Both sachets are unopened, Mausi. The fresh milk Billu brought had only saffron in it.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] Get up, Aditya. The act is over.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [quietly] Billu, I kept the blood off your hands. Mausi was the one putting it on.

beats.action: Set-up 1 (l13): two-shot, Mausi steps close to Kiran, faces near, warm. Set-up 2 (l14): insert, hands only: Mausi's green-bangled hand closes on Kiran's LEFT wrist. Set-up 3 (first sentence of l15), the end state in one still: Mausi's green-bangled hand holding the chooda pushed up the palm-down left forearm; Kiran's fingers open; the two folds already on the sheet below, by the notebook. The paper ticks in sfx_notes carry the drop. Set-up 4 (rest of l15, from 'The hand you were searching for' through 'came to do'): insert, the crescent scar bare in the lamplight on the outer forearm below the pushed-up cuff, exactly as in story_locks.scar and the hand sheet. The 1.2 s silence after l15: Aditya single, looking at it. Kiran does not pull away.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [quietly] You were fourteen. Burnt on a hot iron tawa in your uncle's kitchen.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] I tied the bandage myself, meri bachchi.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] Do look, Damaad ji. The hand you were searching for. This is it. [quietly] Now do what you came to do.

beats.action: The 1.8 s silence before the lines is two set-ups: insert on the sheet beside Aditya: the notebook beside him has fallen open; the creased photograph lies half out of it, the bride's hand and the same crescent showing, the two unopened folds beside it. Then Aditya's face, his eyes going from the print to her arm. His hands are empty on his knees: no phone, no notebook, no lock. l16 on Aditya single, REUSE of the silence's Aditya frame (or a 1.3x punch-in on it). l17 on Kiran single, chin level, left forearm still bare; she does not pull the bangles down. l32 plays over the same Kiran single after l17, Aditya off screen (heard_as off_screen): no new shot. That single now holds about 6 s; if a measured take pushes it past 8 s, S7 holds it on its camera move.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] You.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] Yes. Me.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] The hand I came to kill kept me alive tonight.

beats.action: Set-up 1 (the 0.8 s silence, l18): insert, Kiran's hand unhooking the steel key ring from Mausi's LEFT hip. Set-up 2 (l19): two-shot, Mausi lets her, almost amused. Set-up 3 (tail of l19): insert, Kiran knotting the ring at her own left hip, at the saree's waist. Set-up 4 (l20): Billu single, toothpick gone, asking Kiran, not Mausi. Set-up 5 (l21): Kiran single; the window grille behind her has greyed toward dawn.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] I'll keep the accounts now, Mausi.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [chuckles] Go on, take them. They get heavy, beta.

lines.speaker: billu
lines.text: [nervous] And what about Mausi?

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] No more weddings for Mausi. She'll sit at the bureau and write the accounts.

beats.action: The 0.8 s silence before the lines is its own frame: first grey light in the open iron-sheet front door at the foot of the flight, the landing bulb still on. Set-up 1 (l22 only): two-shot on the stairs, Aditya a step below Kiran, sandals on, glasses, key on its red thread. Kiran holds the creased photograph and the small black notebook flat against her body in her right hand, the print's back to camera; her left forearm is still bare. Set-up 2 (l23): Kiran single. Set-up 3 (l24 and l34): insert, the creased print held flat against her body in her right hand, on the closed notebook, back to camera. Set-up 4 (l25): Aditya single, looking up at her. Set-up 5 (l26): Kiran single, REUSE of the set-up 2 frame. Set-up 6 (l27): over Kiran's shoulder, Aditya below on the flight already turned down toward the grey doorway, his back to her. No apology is spoken.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] I am going to the police, Kiran.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] Go. What will you put in the complaint? That your wife ran off?

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [quietly] Mohit didn't file one either.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] And this photo stays with me now.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] You could have gone.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [sighs] Where to?

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] Go home, Aditya. Open your shop.

beats.action: Dawn grey, no line. Two set-ups of about 2.2 s and 2.3 s. Set-up 1: Aditya alone in the empty lane, cream kurta, glasses, the brass key on its red thread for a lock that no longer exists, nothing else in his hands (no phone, no notebook, no photograph); he looks up once at the first-floor window with its iron grille, the lamp still lit, nobody at it. Set-up 2: Billu's old white sedan under the dead streetlight; through the rear side window Mausi in the back seat, hands in her lap, nothing at her hip; Billu only as a hand on the wheel; Kiran is in the front passenger seat, out of frame (never shown in b8). The engine starts as sound.

Bureau front room, day 2 evening: tube light, blue dusk at the roll-down shutter, shut to customers. Time overlay: 'Evening' (the Hindi cut's overlay reads 'शाम'). Set-up 1 (the 1.6 s silence): Mausi at the desk at the back of the room, writing in the red ledger, no keys at her hip; in the foreground, face out of frame, Kiran in the grey salwar-kurta, the key ring at her left hip, her bare left forearm with the crescent in the tube light. Set-up 2 (l28): Chhoti on the low wooden cot along the right wall, chooda on both forearms, phone in the pink cover in her right hand; in her left fingers a paper fold held over a steel glass of milk on a steel tray beside her. She giggles at Kiran; the fold trembles.

lines.speaker: chhoti
lines.text: [chuckles] Didi, tomorrow's my first wedding. Like a film, right?

beats.action: Kiran does not answer Chhoti. Set-up 1 (l29): insert, Kiran's LEFT hand, hennaed, palm down, the forearm bare with the crescent on its outer side in the tube light, closes over Chhoti's left hand and holds it still. Set-up 2 (l30): two-shot, Kiran and Chhoti in profile on the cot; Kiran level and warm, in Mausi's unhurried rhythm. Set-up 3, final image (the 1.8 s silence after l30): the two hands over the glass, the powder falling into the milk; behind them, soft focus, Mausi at the desk with the ledger and no keys. Cut to black.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [quietly] Don't let your hand shake.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] Pour in the whole sachet, Chhoti. Half doesn't put them to sleep.

sfx_notes: Bed, b1 to b6: a shut lane before dawn, the lamp's faint hum, one dog far off. No rain.
b1: Mausi's keys chink once as she half turns on l02; the frame is Billu, so the chink alone carries her turn.
b2: Billu's sneakers on the concrete floor; a boot shifts by the door; the car key's steel ring ticks once on his finger on the key insert.
b3: marigold garlands rustle and the bed creaks as Aditya sits up; two pairs of boots step back on concrete toward the door.
b4: green glass bangles clink as Mausi grips the wrist; the chooda's dry slide up the forearm; two tiny paper ticks as the folds land on the sheet. Duck the bed under l15.
b6: the key ring unhooked from Mausi's hip, a long chink; a shorter chink as Kiran knots it at her own.
b7: stairwell echo, sandals on concrete steps, first birds through the open front door.
b8: dawn birds; Billu's car ignition turns, catches and idles, then pulls away. Nothing else.
b9: tube light hum; a ballpoint scratching on ledger paper from the desk, continuous under the scene.
b10: a paper tap on the fold, a soft hiss of powder into milk. The bed and music duck right down under l30 so every word is clear; after l30 only the pen scratch, then cut.
music_note: No score in b1 to b3. A low single-note drone enters on the wrist grab in b4 and holds through b5, gone by b6. b6 to b8 are sound only. A faint lullaby-like phrase enters under b9, ducks under l30 and ends unresolved on the final image.
ending_question: Kiran now owns the life she wanted out of: will Chhoti pour in the whole sachet at her first wedding tomorrow?
writer_notes: English adaptation of script.hi.json (S5), not a literal translation. Same beats, same speakers, same line ids in the same play order (l31 still sits between l04 and l05), same emotion tags on every line, same silent_seconds and silent_position per beat. Sources: script.hi.json, bible.json (register.english_version, voice_note_en, one_word_per_object, the s1e01 anchor line in English), D-007 directions 1 and 12.

action, on_screen, location, sfx_notes and music_note are the Hindi script's, shared between both cuts, with these changes only: the quoted cue words in action are the English words that land on the cut ('Come, beta' in b1; 'Mohit's' and 'car' in b2; 'The fresh milk Billu brought' in b3; 'The hand you were searching for' and 'came to do' in b4), and the b9 time overlay reads 'Evening'. The D-024 action edits (b3, b4, b5, b7: which line plays over which shot) mirror the Hindi file's. Characters' name fields are Latin only and voice_note describes the Indian English accent for each speaker, from the bible's voice_note_en.

One word per object, from the bible: sachet for पुड़िया, accounts for हिसाब (l03, l18, l21), car for गाड़ी, milk for दूध, chooda unchanged. 'Tola' and 'tawa' are kept as Indian English speakers say them. Mausi keeps beta, Damaad ji and meri bachchi; Chhoti keeps Didi. The Hindi tag 'ना' in l28 becomes 'right?' rather than 'na', which an English voice may misread (as in the proof).

Locked and directed lines in English: l18 'I'll keep the accounts now, Mausi.' is the bible's b6 line. l15 keeps the b4 anchor ('the hand you were searching for, this is it'). l30 echoes the English anchor of s1e01 b1, 'Pour in the whole sachet. Half doesn't put me to sleep.', as an echo not a copy (D-007 direction 12): 'them' points at the grooms, and 'put to sleep' keeps the Hindi's doubt over whether the full dose sedates or kills. 'You taught me this' and 'the boy turned out weak' are not spoken. l25/l26 pair 'gone' with 'Where to?'.

Length (D-024 ruling 4; the 1,050 measure is withdrawn): 34 lines, about 1,422 dialogue characters without tags (the earlier 1,210 hand count plus 178 for the D-024 pass plus 34 for C1 round 2). Targets keep the first adaptation's sizing (about 13 characters a second for Kiran, Aditya and Billu, about 11.5 for Mausi, a floor for one- and two-word turns). Spoken targets 117.9 s, 22 speaker changes x 0.3 s = 6.6 s, silences 16.2 s: 140.7 s on targets. The projection in clarity_pass (137.3 s) is the figure to use. Trim order if the measured English cut passes 150 s: the Hindi file's, silences only (b8 4.5 s to 3.5 s, then b3 2.0 s to 1.5 s, then b5 1.8 s to 1.4 s); every line is a ledger carrier, protected or a clarity line, so no line is listed for trimming.

Lines outside about 15 per cent of the Hindi target, all short, not padded: l06 2.0 s against 2.4 s; l24 2.4 s against 3.0 s (it shares its insert frame with l34 now); l32 4.0 s against 4.8 s (it shares the Kiran single with l17, so no frame is left short). l33 (2.6 against 3.0) and l34 (2.8 against 3.2) sit just inside. All other lines are within about 15 per cent. Longest single-frame holds after the D-024 pass, estimated from the English take-1 rate (about 13 characters a second): b3 set-up 2 (second sentence of l11 plus l33, 84 characters) about 6.5 s; b4 set-up 4 (rest of l15, 72 characters at Mausi's slower pace) about 6 s; b5 Kiran single (l17, a speaker change, l32) about 6 s; b7 set-up 3 (l24 plus l34) about 5 s. l21 and l01 stay single-frame holds of about 4.5 s and 3.6 s measured. None is expected past 8 s; S7 checks against the takes and splits with a 1.3x punch-in if one does.

Short turns flagged for extra takes: l31 'Twelve.', l16 'You.', l17 'Yes. Me.', l26 'Where to?'. If l16 is unstable after three takes, the voice director may try '[quietly] You... it was you.' with the subtitle changed to match. [sharply] on l08 means low and fast, not loud. No whispers; l30 is [calm] and unfiltered with the bed ducked under it.

Pronunciation dictionary candidates for the English voices: tola (TOH-laa), tawa (TAH-vaa), beta (BAY-taa), Damaad ji (da-MAAD jee), meri bachchi (MAY-ree BUCH-chee), Didi (DEE-dee), Chhoti (CHHO-tee), Kiran (KI-run), Aditya (AA-dit-yaa), Mohit (MO-hit), Billu (BIL-loo), Mausi (MAU-see).

Not verified: this session has no shell, so the JSON was not run through a parser, and the id match against script.hi.json, the tag lists, the character count and the timing sums were checked by hand only. No line has been voiced; every target_seconds is an estimate. The tags are the Hindi script's (all from the proof set); whether each cast voice obeys them in English is not confirmed.

D-024 clarity pass (S5, 26 Nov): mirrors the Hindi pass in script.hi.json exactly. The pre-pass English is kept in script.en.prev.json. 27 lines are byte-identical to the pre-pass English (text, tags and target), so their English takes stay valid; l02 gains only heard_as. Reworded: l07, l11, l15, l28. Added: l33 (b3, after l11), l32 (b5, after l17), l34 (b7, after l24), with the Hindi ids. The cold viewer's English-side faults for s1b03 in docs/clarity-cold-viewers.md (saffron against the poured powder, 'Aditya' named late, the dropped vow, Mausi's motive) are the same faults the Hindi pass fixes, and no unchanged English line was flagged there, so no English-only reword was made. New Kiran lines take [calm], not [quietly]: the takes file records that Kiran's English [quietly] came out whispered in casting. Mausi's added sentence in l15 keeps the Hindi's [quietly]; her English [quietly] takes (l10, l13) are voiced. The 'Not verified' note above is the first adaptation's and holds for this pass too: no parser was run and the new and reworded lines are not voiced.

C1 round 2 (S5, 26 Nov): mirrors the S2 round-2 rewording of l04, l31, l05 and l09 in script.hi.json and adds one English-only gloss in l13. l04 now names s1b02's own wedding in s1b02's English words ('Last party', 'twenty-two tola'; s1b02 l07 'Last party brought twenty-two tola'), and Billu's l31 'Twelve.' repeats s1b02 l08 'Twelve. Mausi said so.', so the figures no longer clash. 'Say it in front of Mausi.' is the Hindi 'मौसी के सामने बोल' and gives the reason Kiran says it a second time. l05 drops the ordinal 'The sixth' for 'Before that', as the Hindi drops 'छठी'; 'Mohit's' stays as the cue word for the b2 Aditya insert. l09 now asks Mausi to confirm, so l10 'The poor child is tired, Billu.' dodges a direct question. l13 'a hot iron tawa' glosses tawa inside the line: Hindi needs no gloss, so the id stays paired and only the English text changes. 'party' needs no new gloss: it is glossed on both paths in shared s1e01 l14 (viewer ledger terms) and used in s1b02 l07. No beat, shot, frame, tag or heard_as changed.

lines.before: [quietly] I kept the blood off your hands. Mausi was the one putting it on.
lines.after: [quietly] Billu, I kept the blood off your hands. Mausi was the one putting it on.
